title: Compatibility Testing Across Ruby Versions
learning_outcomes: Explain the role of compatibility testing across ruby versions in a Ruby program and name the key rule involved.
Apply compatibility testing across ruby versions in a small example and predict its result before running it.
Identify one boundary or failure case related to identifying unintended behavior changes and verify the intended behavior.

content.intro: Learn Compatibility Testing Across Ruby Versions through a visual model, a minimal Ruby example, and a practical check.
content.why_it_matters: Understanding compatibility testing across ruby versions helps you write code that is easier to explain, test, and maintain. It also helps separate Ruby language guarantees from runtime assumptions, dependency behavior, and application-specific rules.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: Compatibility Testing Across Ruby Versions helps you reason about runtime version matrices. In Ruby, prefer a small example whose inputs and expected result are easy to explain. This lesson connects the syllabus topic to practical code and highlights where assumptions or edge cases matter.

content_blocks.title: How to think about it
content_blocks.text: Begin by identifying the key rule: Runtime version matrices. Then connect it to Dependency compatibility. The remaining syllabus points—Version-specific test failures, Identifying unintended behavior changes—are useful checks before applying this in a larger project.

content_blocks.title: Example: Compatibility Testing Across Ruby Versions
content_blocks.code:
minimum_supported = Gem::Version.new("3.2")
current = Gem::Version.new(RUBY_VERSION)
puts(current >= minimum_supported)
content_blocks.expected_output: true for the course baseline; verify the declared support range.

items.title: Assuming the happy path is enough
items.text: Test an empty value, a boundary value, and one invalid value before depending on the behavior.

items.title: Treating an example as a universal rule
items.text: Check Ruby version, runtime implementation, and third-party library documentation when behavior is version-sensitive.

items.title: Mixing too many concerns
items.text: Separate input parsing, domain behavior, and output so each piece is easier to test.

content_blocks.title: Guided example
content_blocks.text: Run the example as written, compare it with the expected result, and explain why each line supports compatibility testing across ruby versions. Next change one input or condition and predict the result before running it.

content_blocks.title: Recap
content_blocks.text: You should now be able to explain compatibility testing across ruby versions, identify its place in ruby internals, native extensions, and legacy maintenance, run a focused example, and verify an important boundary. Revisit the linked exercise if this is a core topic; advanced runtime or framework examples remain draft until reviewed in a suitable environment.
